title: Clover's Winking Lantern
markdown:
In the Starberry Hills, where the sun painted the clouds like fluffy sheep and the air smelled sweet as a honeybee’s hug, lived a young witch named Clover. Her little cottage peeked from behind berry bushes and held a gentle glow even when the moon was the only light. Inside, a kettle knew the hour by the way the light sat on the sill. Eyes like shiny dewdrops. A heart that hummed with soft magic. She was learning to be a witch, just like her Grandma Meadowsweet, whose chimney puffed shapes of happy butterflies, and whose polishing cloth still hung on Clover’s peg, worn soft at the corners.

Near Clover, under a whispering willow, lived a young wizard named Elio Star. Hair that sparkled like the first star of the evening. A voice like wind chimes. They were the best of friends, even though they learned different kinds of sparkle-magic. They played in the meadows, chasing dandelion fluff. They listened to sleepy bumblebees. And always nearby was Flicker, a tiny pony no bigger than a happy dog. Coat soft like a grey cloud. Little hooves, tap-tap-tap on the moss. Big brown eyes that saw every little thing.

Today was a very special day. The annual Lantern Polishing Contest, held in the blackberry hollow, which always smelled like sweet jam left in the sun. Clover felt a little flutter in her tummy. She wished with all her heart to win. She imagined Grandma Meadowsweet’s smile, warm as a summer sunrise, the sort of smile that could make shy violets bloom. Deep inside, a little worry hid, like a shy field mouse. Clover’s magic, she thought, was not as bright as Elio’s. What if her lantern did not shine enough? What if Elio’s shone like a rainbow, and hers only blinked? The worry felt like a tiny bumpy stone in her shoe.

Flicker, with a happy wiggle, wanted to be part of the fun too.

The contest was only once a year. If Clover did not polish her lantern today, she would wait a whole year for another chance. She really wanted to see Grandma Meadowsweet’s happy smile this year.

So Clover and Elio, with polishing cloths and special lanterns, went to the blackberry hollow. The path wiggled down past ferns that tickled their knees. Cool air whispered from under the mountain. Blackberry bushes hung heavy with berries, plump and dark as little jewels. Flicker trotted beside them, tail swishing like a friendly flag. This was the first time the contest sat so deep in the hollow. Everything felt new. Damp earth. Sweet dark fruit. A warm hug of a smell.

Other lanterns were already arriving, little moons coming down the path. Someone had set out a table of jam tarts that nobody was eating yet, because polishing came first. They found a smooth flat rock, cool and solid under their feet.

“Ready?” Elio asked, eyes twinkling.

Clover nodded. Her heart tap-danced against her ribs. Her paws felt a little clammy. She tried a new charm to make her lantern extra bright. Instead, the lantern gave a little flicker-pop, and a tiny puff of lavender smoke appeared, smelling of sleepy fields. The magic went out like a candle. Clover felt a prickle of tears. She almost dropped her polishing cloth. She wanted to hide behind a big fern.

Just then Flicker nudged Clover’s lantern with his nose, leaving a tiny damp spot. Then he gave Elio’s a gentle boop. Tap-tap-tap on the rock. A streak of polish from Elio’s cloth landed on Flicker’s nose.

Achoo.

Flicker sneezed a small cloud of glittery polish dust, sparkling like a miniature constellation. Clover giggled. Elio laughed, a sound like tiny bells. The lavender smoke tickled Flicker’s nose. He gave a funny little snort, tail wiggling. Clover’s worry began to feel less heavy, like a cloud breaking apart. Elio was wiping glitter off his cheek, and he was laughing too.

As they polished and giggled, the lanterns began to shine. Clover’s did not have a perfectly steady glow. It had little bursts of soft lavender light that winked on and off, like happy fireflies. Elio’s had a bright steady beam, like a captured moonbeam. Both were beautiful. Clover’s lantern was not wrong. It was hers. Playful puffs of smoke. Winking lights that seemed to tell little stories. Flicker, with a delightful smudge of polish on his nose, looked very pleased, tail bobbing.

A tiny whisper of worry tried to sneak in. Winning was the only thing that mattered, it said. A little knot in her chest. But Elio’s kind smile, and Flicker’s happy snorts, made the knot loosen. She took a deep breath. She imagined the tiny pebble in her shoe melting into a warm drop of sunshine. She thought of Grandma Meadowsweet’s smile. She thought of Elio’s bright lantern. Then she let her warmest giggle float toward her own. A tiny puff of warmth, smelling faintly of berries, rose from her chest into the lantern. Her chest felt a little lighter, like a balloon with a little air let out.

As the sun dipped behind the high rocks, long shadows like sleepy cats, it was time to go home. Clover and Elio picked up their lanterns. One winking and soft. One bright and steady. Flicker trotted between them. Soft powdery snow began to fall, not cold, wrapping the world like a quiet blanket. The lanterns made little pools of light on the snowy path.

Back in her cozy cottage, Clover put her lantern on her bedside table. It winked a soft lavender light. She smiled, a big smile that reached her eyes. She no longer felt the worry flutter. Later, as the snow fell, a tiny flicker of doubt tried to sneak in, like a little shadow under the kettle. Then she remembered her warm giggle and the happy glow her lantern now had. A soft tap-tap-tap outside her window. Elio, holding his own lantern, snow in his sparkling hair.

“Want to share some warm starberry cocoa?” he whispered.

Clover nodded. She poured two mugs. The cocoa steamed, berry-dark and sweet. Flicker stood at the door with polish still on his nose, and she let him in for a carrot and a warm patch of floor. The lantern winked. Elio’s beam sat steady beside it, moon and firefly sharing a table. Flicker’s hooves made a last small rhythm, and then the hills went quiet, the way hills do when friends have come home.
characters: Clover (young witch), Elio Star (young wizard), Flicker (tiny pony)
author: StoryGen Community
